newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. body targets Israeli building in E. Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: U.N. body targets Israeli building in E. Jerusalem.

text.p: The General Assembly holds a debate on Wednesday that is expected to end with the adoption of a resolution by an overwhelming majority calling on Israel to abandon plans for a new Jewish neighbourhood in mainly Arab East Jerusalem.

The Assembly is being summoned into session at the request of the Arab group of states in reaction to the vetoing by the United States last Friday of a similar resolution in the Security Council which won the support of the 14 other council members.

The United States, like the almost 50 other speakers in the council debate, was criticial of the Israeli action but said the U.N. body was not an appropriate forum for dealing with issues under negotiation between the two parties.
There is no veto in the 185-member General Assembly, whose resolutions are not binding.

At issue is an Israeli decision to build 6,500 homes for Jews on a tree-covered hill between East Jerusalem and Bethlehem, called Har Homa by Israel and Jabal Abu Ghneim by the Palestinians, that Israel captured during the 1967 Middle East war.

Relations between the two sides were further exacerbated, and the Middle East peace process brought to a standstill, after Israel announced last Friday it would withdraw from nine percent of the West Bank in the first of three scheduled pullbacks while the Palestinians said they had expected closer to 30 percent.
